question: across every money / bond / convertible ETF in the panel: which carry a print that is both r2046's flip shape and large against that instrument's own daily movement, what does neutralising those do to its annualised return, and does r2046's repair stay inside the one shelf that earned it

flip_rule.treatment: both bars booked at exactly zero return; pair listed in quote_audit
flip_rule.why: r2041's repair is a 35% rule and the money reader zeroes drops > 50bp but keeps the rebound; a sub-threshold quote flip therefore lands as a fake gain

sigma_rule.definition: |drop_bp| / (that instrument's daily return std in bp, same window)
sigma_rule.why: the frozen geometry is an absolute -50bp; on a money ETF with a 4bp daily sigma that is 12 sigma, on a convertible ETF with a 65bp sigma it is a normal move. Repairing by shape alone would move 511380's annualised return by more than a percentage point in the wrong direction.
sigma_rule.this_is_not: a significance test; it is the readability floor for 'not a market move'

ruler.why: this face describes the quote series, not a trade; the entry cost is the same bar in both branches and cancels in the difference

adoption.note: no second budget or ticket is declared here; both are read and printed
